# SakanaAI/AI-Scientist — pinned source assessment

**Source:** https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist at [`1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb`](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/commit/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb) (committed 2025-12-19). The ignored checkout is `references/work/sakana-ai-scientist/`; it is not a runtime dependency. This is an external technique source, not evidence of Google's Co-Scientist implementation.

## Terms and reuse boundary

The pinned root [LICENSE](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/LICENSE) is **The AI Scientist Source Code License**, version 1.0 (December 2025), not MIT. It grants conditional reproduction, derivative-work, and distribution rights. Distribution of the contribution requires the full license, and its restrictions and downstream terms include a prominent AI-generation disclosure for scientific manuscripts, papers, or technical reports produced using that software. The tracked tree contains no second `LICENSE`, `COPYING`, or `NOTICE` file. A bundled [Tensorf helper](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/templates/tensorf/dataLoader/colmap2nerf.py#L3-L9) separately reserves NVIDIA's rights and prohibits use, reproduction, or distribution without an express agreement. No bundled template, source, or prompt is approved for copying. Independently implemented techniques require a distinct local acceptance case and source-idea attribution.

## Source shape and operating assumptions

The checkout has 2,326 tracked files: 15 under `ai_scientist/`, 25 under `review_ai_scientist/`, 1,028 under `review_iclr_bench/`, 1,107 example-paper artifacts, and 136 template files. No tracked Python test module matches the repository's `test*.py` or `tests/` pattern; the benchmark and example artifacts require separate inspection before treating them as validation. The pinned [README](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/README.md) describes a Linux/NVIDIA CUDA/PyTorch workflow, LaTeX, code-editing experiments, and frontier-model API credentials. It recommends GPT-4o for review, reports model-specific positive bias and formatting failures, and describes roughly $15 per generated paper. The optional Semantic Scholar key and experimental no-key OpenAlex route do not make the overall workflow free. No upstream setup, agent workflow, model, or benchmark command has been run, and no campaign credential was supplied to the checkout.

The authors' [paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2408.06292v3) reports automated-review performance on 500 ICLR 2022 OpenReview papers (65% versus 66% balanced accuracy in its comparison) and describes 10 novelty-search rounds, 5 review reflections, and 5 ensembled reviews in its experimental setup. It reports that ensembling did not substantially improve accuracy, although it reduced variance, and its calibrated reviewer had a higher false-positive rate than the human comparison (0.31 versus 0.17). The authors also note possible training-data overlap, camera-ready/submission differences, overestimated self-assessed novelty, unfair experimental comparisons, and invented results. These are results and limitations for machine-learning manuscripts, not verified gains in our hypothesis-level scientific workflow. Any local adoption must be evaluated at the appropriate Co-Scientist boundary under the campaign's fixed inputs and zero-cost model policy.

## Implemented architecture and inspection map

The standard [launcher](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/launch_scientist.py#L343-L420) generates a template-conditioned idea batch, checks novelty, saves `ideas.json`, runs experiments for selected ideas, writes LaTeX papers, and requests reviews. Idea generation and reflection are prompt-driven in [generate_ideas.py](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/ai_scientist/generate_ideas.py#L14-L174). Its [novelty loop](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/ai_scientist/generate_ideas.py#L285-L492) asks the model for Semantic Scholar or OpenAlex queries, exposes up to ten search results per query, and eventually asks for a free-form Boolean novelty verdict. It can search repeatedly, but the idea record does not provide a structured per-claim prior-art audit or calibrated novelty score. The experimental open-ended launcher has an [archive-conditioned idea path](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/ai_scientist/generate_ideas.py#L178-L272); unlike the standard path, it [does not gate the newest idea on novelty](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/experimental/launch_oe_scientist.py#L359-L394). These are distinct shipped paths, not interchangeable claims about a single invariant.

The [experiment executor](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/ai_scientist/perform_experiments.py#L12-L165) uses Aider to edit `experiment.py`, executes the revised code as a subprocess, gathers metric means and standard errors, and feeds the results back into planning, plotting, and notes. That requires a writable code template and GPU-oriented local runtime; it is not a general scientific-verification or safety layer. State is primarily per-idea JSON, snapshots, and result folders, without the current product's durable task and append-only lineage contracts. The [reviewer](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/ai_scientist/perform_review.py#L126-L243) can sample multiple same-model reviews, aggregate numeric scores through a meta-review, and reflect on the result; the standard launcher [hard-codes GPT-4o](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/launch_scientist.py#L263-L280) for this step. Review parsing has a visible [all-invalid-samples failure path](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/ai_scientist/perform_review.py#L163-L175); this is an assessment of its contract, not a claim from a live experiment.

Its [ICLR benchmark](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/review_iclr_bench/iclr_analysis.py#L170-L205) compares binary Accept/Reject labels with accuracy, F1, hard-label ROC AUC, and false-positive/negative rates. It does not measure biomedical hypothesis novelty, citation support, or scientific correctness. The cached reviews and example papers are artifacts, not a unit-test suite; running the benchmark can invoke paid providers. [Paper writing and citation insertion](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/ai_scientist/perform_writeup.py#L220-L487) serve autonomous paper production, which is outside this campaign's product scope. The alternative OpenAlex search record does not supply the `citationStyles` field that this citation-insertion path reads, so the two paths should not be treated as one proven end-to-end connector.

## Comparison with the current product

Our durable run executes independent review and evidence tasks, Elo pairwise ranking, deep verification, recurrent meta-review, and append-only hypothesis lineage ([workflow map](../../docs/EXPLAINER.md), [fan-out](../../app/app/engine_tasks_fanout.py)). This is the **Google-backed requirement** boundary; Sakana's paper-generation pipeline does not alter it. A local literature-tool path [searches once per draft](../../engine/src/co_scientist/agents/generation/literature_tools/validate_novelty.py) and [analyzes papers before synthesis](../../engine/src/co_scientist/agents/generation/literature_tools/validate_stages.py); ordinary review instead explicitly marks its novelty score as [prior-knowledge judgment](../../engine/src/co_scientist/prompts/templates/review.md), without claiming a search. The broader literature review can perform a budgeted follow-up search, and deep reviews gather claim-specific evidence, but those do not establish result-conditioned *per-draft* query refinement. Sakana's repeated-query loop is an **external technique** that is only partially covered locally; its terminal Boolean is model-declared, does not expose a per-claim evidence ledger, and turns exhausted search errors into `novel = False`. Making that Boolean an always-on publication gate would be a **local design choice** without supporting evaluation.

Our initial review, mature cascade, one-time blocked-idea recheck, recurrent review, and Elo tournament already yield multiple distinct judgments, while the app persists their artifacts ([review node](../../engine/src/co_scientist/agents/reflection/review.py), [gate](../../engine/src/co_scientist/agents/reflection/review_gate.py), [ranking parity](../../docs/PARITY.md)). Sakana's ensemble resamples the *same model* for a paper Accept/Reject decision; it is neither independent expert voting nor a replacement for the paper-backed Elo system. Its own paper found no material accuracy increase from ensembling. The local `call_llm_json` boundary retries and validates structured output; Sakana's all-invalid review-sample indexing failure is not a reliability pattern to import.

Our simulation review can execute a bounded computational model in an available sandbox, and a researcher can append measured outcomes with protocol, conditions, controls, interpretation, and evidence IDs ([simulation](../../engine/src/co_scientist/agents/reflection/simulation_execution.py), [outcome store](../../app/app/store/outcomes.py)). Outcomes are visible after publication, but current [report assembly](../../app/app/report_build.py) does not feed them to the engine; the run is not automatically restarted from a new outcome. Sakana's feedback is from edits to its *own* `experiment.py` and template-specific metrics, followed by autonomous replanning. Importing that behavior would add the separate computational-discovery runtime this campaign excludes. The local evolution and meta-review already condition new hypotheses on prior hypothesis/review state; archive-conditioned proposal alone is covered. Autonomous LaTeX paper production is out of scope; the existing report has provenance and safety gates.

## Candidate decisions

All costs below are additional campaign costs. No upstream model or benchmark call was made. Source links above are pinned; local counterparts are linked in the comparison.

| ID and affected behavior | Fidelity and reuse approach | Acceptance criterion and test boundary | Evaluation, cost, disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **M7-NOV-01**: refine a per-draft prior-art query from retrieved results to find relevant work a first search misses. | **External technique**, partially covered; independently implement inside the existing optional validation path if useful. The local per-draft validator searches once, while the source feeds results back into subsequent query selection. | Freeze public draft hypotheses and known prior art before comparison. Primary metric: relevant prior-art recall beyond the first-query result set; non-regressions: citation provenance, false rejection of genuinely distinct ideas, bounded requests, and zero-price model routing. Compare fixed baseline/candidate at the engine retrieval/workflow boundary, beginning with three paired trials if a change is implemented. | **Open, promising but inconclusive.** The source demonstrates the loop, not a matched biomedical gain. First establish a concrete local retrieval miss on fixed public inputs; then adopt or reject from that evidence. No extra calls or spend yet. |
| **M7-REV-02**: same-model review ensemble for more stable scientific judgments. | **External technique**; independent implementation would multiply local review calls while retaining Elo and safety semantics. | Fixed hypothesis/evidence cases, primary claim-support or ranking-concordance metric, no safety/citation regression, paired live trials at identical zero-price settings; engine review/ranking boundary. | The authors report lower variance but no material ICLR binary-decision accuracy gain; their benchmark does not transfer to hypothesis quality, and their measured false-positive rate is higher than the human comparator. Five samples plus meta-review multiply calls without demonstrated campaign benefit. **Rejected** on current evidence; no paid or free inference spent. |
| **M7-EXP-03**: feed executed experiment metrics into automated replanning. The local product records human-measured outcomes but does not steer the completed run from them. | **External technique** tied to Aider-edited `experiment.py`, writable templates, subprocesses, and GPU execution. Reusing it would require a new computational-discovery runtime rather than a compatible adapter. | An authorized continuation feature would need lineage-preserving outcome ingestion, sandbox safety, fixed outcome-to-hypothesis examples, and durable API/engine verification. No such feature is in this campaign's authorized boundary. | Local simulation and append-only measured outcomes already serve the existing workflow; Sakana does not provide a directly reusable post-publication outcome loop. **Outside authorized scope**; do not copy code or start experiments. |
| **M7-ARCH-04**: condition later proposals on earlier ideas/results. | **External technique**; local evolution and recurrent meta-review already condition on the existing pool and prior evaluations. | A change would need to preserve append-only parent lineage and improve fixed-pool diversity without hurting evidence, tested at the engine workflow boundary. | Source has no matched evidence of a local gap beyond the existing context feed. **Already covered**; no change or added calls. |
| **M7-PAPER-05**: generate a LaTeX paper and automatic ICLR review. | **External technique** requiring template/code experiments and manuscript publication. | Outside the existing Co-Scientist report-publication boundary. | Current reports already carry evidence, safety gating, and provenance; independent paper production is an explicit non-goal. **Outside authorized scope**. |
| **M7-NOV-06**: turn every model-declared novelty Boolean into a default publication gate. | **Local design choice** based on the source's terminal Boolean, not a Google-backed requirement. | Would require calibrated known/novel cases, failure-as-unknown semantics, source-linked audit, and no material false-reject regression at the report-publication boundary. | The source has no such calibration or per-claim trail, and exhausted search errors become `novel = False`; ordinary local review already avoids claiming an unsearched idea is unprecedented. **Rejected** as a default gate, independently of M7-NOV-01. |

No candidate is yet accepted for code changes. M7-NOV-01 remains open until its retrieval usefulness is tested; this is not yet a closed no-product-change repository assessment. The source's positive review metrics and novelty verdicts are not local scientific-quality evidence. After that decision, verify the intended release or the unchanged deployment as appropriate; do not force a redundant deployment for a documented no-change outcome.
